notes: Summary: Enterprise procurement focused on Redwood Dedicated. Primary ask = hard throughput guarantees + clear SLA credit schedule. Very cost-conscious but will pay for predictable performance.
Workload profile: mix of synchronous chat (low-latency P95 needs) + large-scale reranking for search pipelines during market open spikes. Spiky QPS; need burst capacity + reserved baseline.

Throughput/Reserved GPU ask: planning for baseline 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with ability to burst to 12 for 30m windows during peak market events. Want explicit throughput guarantees expressed as tokens/sec and concurrent request capacity.

Latency SLOs: pushing for p95 < 80ms for short-chat (<=128 tokens) and p99 < 350ms overall; Redwood proposed p95 < 60ms but team concerned about tail under load. Need definition whether SLO measured at model response or at app-level (includes network).

Uptime & credits: Northcrest legal wants 99.95% monthly uptime. Redwood proposed 99.9% default with 10% service credits for month below 99.9%, 25% below 99.5%. Northcrest counter: 99.95% with graduated credits (5% for 99.9-99.95, 15% for 99.5-99.9, 40% below 99.5). AE/SE to propose middle ground (99.93% + faster credit payout).

Maintenance windows: Northcrest requires scheduled maintenance <= 2 hours per quarter and pre-notice >= 21 days for non-emergency; Redwood standard is monthly 4-hour window with 72h notice. This is a major negotiation point.

Support/Response times: Northcrest wants P1 response <= 15 minutes (initial ack) and resolution SLA for critical production incidents within 4 hours. Redwood's enterprise plan offers 30 min P1 ack and 8 hour target. SE proposed trial of 15 min ack for first 6 months tied to committed spend.
Failover & fallbacks: Must document automated fallback to model variants and cross-region failover; Northcrest needs runbook for degradation modes, and 'graceful degradation' policy in SOW.

Metrics & measurement: insist on telemetry access (token-level logs, per-route latency histograms, tail metrics p99/p999), and shared dashboard. Also require monthly run-rate testing to validate throughput guarantees.

POC / timeline: 2-week performance POC (loadgen sim of market-open spikes) completed 2026-02-18. Results: average throughput met baseline; p99 tail > target under synthetic burst. SE recommends KV cache tuning + batching to reduce tail. Next step: follow-up POC with caching enabled.
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-12 call: 'We need contractual certainty around availability and burst capacity — tokenized credits won't help if we're offline at open.'

Cost sensitivity: willing to accept premium for dedicated baseline but wants cap on overage rates and transparent per-token billing for burst usage. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions to reduce unit costs post-deploy.

Legal notes: legal provided redline with strict liability cap and stronger termination for SLA failures; Redwood legal asked for standard limitation of liability language. Procurement call scheduled 2026-03-18.

Action items captured: update SLA draft with 99.93% proposal, include 2h quarterly maintenance concession, trial 15 min P1 ack for 6 months contingent on $ committed ARR, run second POC with caching/quantization profile.
